```{r create-training-dataset}

# --- CREATE TRAINING DATASET FOR TRAINING SPECIES ID MODEL --- #

# Loop through each threshold level to import and process datasets.

for(i in 1:length(threshold_levels)){
  
  # Import training dataset 
  
  training_individuals[[i]] = read.csv(here("..",
                                            "1_data",
                                            paste0("training_threshold_",
                                                   threshold_levels[i],
                                                   ".csv"))) %>%
    
  # Exclude Euglena from training monocultures to prevent misidentification 
  # (Eug was only in autotrophic ecosystems).
    
  filter(species != "Eug") %>%
    
  # Transform Spi te into Spi_te, get rid of the comments, and extract numeric 
  # file identifier from the file name.
    
  mutate(species = case_when(species == "Spi te" ~ "Spi_te",
                             TRUE ~ species),
         comment = NULL,
         file = as.numeric(str_extract(file, "\\d+"))) %>% 
  
  # Remove rows with any NA values to ensure complete cases.
    
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  
  # Reoder columns to make it easier to inspect  
  
  select(file,
         id,
         species,
         N_frames,
         mean_area,
         everything())

}

# Create a dataset excluding the species "Ble" for threshold 13. 
# This is necessary because at threshold 13, we could not eliminate 
# the food source (Chi) for "Ble".

ds_individuals_13 = training_individuals[[1]] %>% 
  filter(species != "Ble")  # Filter out "Ble" species

# Create a dataset including only the species "Ble" for threshold 40. 
# At threshold 40, we successfully eliminated the food source (Chi) 
# for "Ble", allowing for its inclusion in the analysis.

ds_individuals_40 = training_individuals[[2]] %>% 
  filter(species == "Ble")  # Filter for "Ble" species only

# Bind the two previous datasets

training_individuals = rbind(ds_individuals_13,
                             ds_individuals_40)
```

```{r create-predictive-model}

# --- CREATE PREDICTIVE MODEL FOR SPECIES ID --- #
# See the file '04_set_paramaters.Rmd' for a description of these variables. 

species_ID_model = svm(factor(species) ~
                         mean_grey +
                         sd_grey +
                         mean_area +
                         sd_area +
                         mean_perimeter +
                         mean_turning +
                         sd_turning +
                         sd_perimeter +
                         mean_major +
                         sd_major +
                         mean_minor +
                         sd_minor +
                         mean_ar +
                         sd_ar +
                         duration +
                         max_net  +
                         net_disp +
                         net_speed +
                         gross_disp +
                         max_step +
                         min_step +
                         sd_step +
                         sd_gross_speed +
                         max_gross_speed +
                         min_gross_speed ,
                       data = training_individuals,
                       probability = T,
                       na.action = na.pass)
```

```{r show-confusion-matrix}

# --- SHOW CONFUSION MATRIX FOR SPECIES ID --- #

# Create a confusion matrix comparing the fitted species predictions from the 
# SVM model with the actual species labels from the training dataset.

confusion_matrix = table(species_ID_model$fitted, training_individuals$species)

# Create a copy of the confusion matrix to modify for error calculation.

confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros = confusion_matrix

# Set the diagonal elements (true positives) to zero for error calculation.
# This allows us to compute the misclassification errors without counting the 
# correct classifications.

diag(confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros) = 0 

# Calculate the class error for each species.
# Class error is defined as the ratio of misclassified samples to the total 
# samples for each species.

confusion_matrix = cbind(
  confusion_matrix,
  class_error = rowSums(confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros) / 
                rowSums(confusion_matrix)) %>%
  
  # Transform into data frame
  
  as.data.frame() %>%
  
  # Convert class error to percentage and remove the original class_error 
  # column for clarity.
  
  mutate(class_error_percentage = class_error * 100, 
         class_error = NULL)

# Display the confusion matrix

confusion_matrix
```

```{r perform-species-identification}

# --- ID SPECIES --- #

ds_individuals = ds_individuals %>% 
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>%
  mutate(species = as.character(predict(object = species_ID_model, 
                                        ., 
                                        type = "response")),
         
         # Given that autotrophic ecosystems are exclusively composed of 
         # Euglena gracilis (Eug), we can simply designate Eug as the species 
         # for each individual in autotrophic ecosystems.
         
         species = ifelse(trophic_type == "autotrophic", 
                          "Eug", 
                          species)) 

# Test: check number of rows

ecosystems_at_time_points = ds_individuals %>%
              select(ecosystem_ID,
                     time_point) %>%
              unique() %>%
              nrow()

n_ecosystem_at_time_points_missing = 
  (n_ecosystems * length(time_points)) - ecosystems_at_time_points

expect_true(n_ecosystem_at_time_points_missing >= 0)
```
